learning_objective: 🎯 Witness a mother's fierce fight for her child's dignity and truth against rigid bureaucracy, all over a single tiny measurement!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Tao Ying, a working-class mother, rides a bus with her young son Xiao Ye. Children under a certain height ride free. The ticket collector accuses her of trying to evade fare, claiming Xiao Ye is taller than the limit.
Tao Ying isn't fighting over the small coin; she is fighting because the public accusation makes her look like a liar in front of her son. She wants to teach him honesty and integrity.
She goes through a lengthy, frustrating bureaucratic process to get her son officially measured by authorities to prove he was indeed under the height limit by just one centimetre.
When she finally receives official proof and vindication, she chooses not to boast or drag her son back into a public spectacle. Her inner dignity and moral victory matter more than external drama.

fun_activity.title: 📏 The Precision Test
fun_activity.instructions: Use a ruler to see exactly how long 'One Centimetre' is. Imagine going through weeks of paperwork and stress just to prove a measurement that small! Why was it worth it for Tao Ying?

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly explain Tao Ying's profession (a cook in a factory cafeteria) and how her modest background contrasts with her immense moral courage.
📌 Highlight the central theme: a parent's desire to protect their child's moral worldview from the cynicism of the adult world.
📌 Notice how the author satirizes the rigid, unempathetic nature of public transport rules and officialdom.
quick_recap: ⭐ The dispute starts on a crowded public bus over a child's ticket fare.
⭐ Tao Ying is meticulous in her daily life, always trying to present a respectable face despite financial limits.
⭐ The story proves that a person's dignity and character cannot be measured by money or social status.
